answer: Card authorization holds: before an identity can withdraw, a payment processor places a refundable $1 hold on a bank card and returns a fingerprint, a stable hash of the card number. The network allows one identity per fingerprint and refuses prepaid card ranges. Banks already vetted the cardholder, so each extra identity needs another real card account. A timber trader at the wharf running ten bots on one card gets one payout, since all ten share a fingerprint. Limit: a hollow shell firm can order corporate cards in bulk, so business cards get a lower cap.
